issue.title: Investigate slow initial startup time (~15s)
issue.body:
## Context

Initial app startup currently feels too slow. The observed startup time is roughly 15 seconds before the app is ready.

This issue is to investigate where that time is being spent inside `whitenoise-rs` initialization and startup work.

## Details

Areas that look worth profiling first:

- `Whitenoise::initialize_whitenoise()` overall startup path
- startup cache sync work such as `sync_message_cache_on_startup()`
- relay / control-plane initialization
- scheduled task startup
- database migrations or other one-time initialization work
- any blocking network calls or waits happening before the UI can proceed

Questions to answer:

- what are the biggest contributors to the ~15 second startup time
- how much of that cost is local CPU / I/O vs network waiting
- which work is truly required before the app becomes usable
- which work can be deferred until after first render / first usable state
- whether there is a measurable difference between first startup, cold startup, and subsequent launches

## Outcome

Produce a breakdown of startup cost and identify concrete follow-up optimizations.

Possible outcomes:

- move non-critical startup work off the critical path
- defer sync or maintenance tasks until after initial readiness
- add instrumentation / timing logs around initialization phases
- split one-time setup from normal launch work
- open targeted follow-up issues once the hotspots are known

## Additional context

There is already app-side DX work around startup behavior in `marmot-protocol/whitenoise`, but this issue is specifically about the Rust core initialization path because that is likely where a large part of the delay lives.

`git worktree same branch multiple worktrees constraint limitation`

Git worktrees have a key constraint: you cannot check out the same branch in multiple worktrees at the same time. Attempting `git worktree add <path> <branch>` when `<branch>` is already checked out elsewhere fails with an error like "'<Branch>' is already checked out at '<other/location>'".[1][2][3] This limitation prevents conflicts because all worktrees share the same underlying repository and branch refs (e.g.,.git/refs/heads/<branch>). Each worktree has its own HEAD, index, and working directory, but if two worktrees point HEAD to the same branch and one commits, it advances the shared branch ref. The other worktree's index would then mismatch the new commit, leading to confusion or errors when committing from it.[4][5][6] Official docs confirm: "By default, `add` refuses to create a new worktree when `<branch>` is a branch name and is already checked out by another worktree."[1][7][3] Use `--force` to override (risky), or `git checkout --ignore-other-worktrees <branch>` in an existing worktree.[2] Workarounds include detached HEAD checkouts (`git worktree add <path> <commit>` or `git checkout --detach`), allowing multiple worktrees at the same commit without branch locking.[4][5] Git remains single-process oriented, so concurrent operations across worktrees risk corruption.[8]

![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/fe803ca425e08f2909f8cd21fb03cb058c6ba39e24b854f51ae047c3c37d5384.png)

## What changed

FRB codegen runs in whitenoise-rs CI now. Every codeowner push to `master` regenerates the Dart bindings and pushes them to a dedicated `flutter-package` orphan branch. The Flutter app consumes that branch as a normal git dependency.

No more `flutter_rust_bridge_codegen generate` runs on the Flutter side. No more git-rev bumps after Rust API changes.

## Added on master

- `crates/whitenoise-frb/`: the FFI wrapper crate. Workspace member, path dep on the parent `whitenoise` crate. Sources ported from the in-flight `whitenoise.move-frb-out` branch (post-singleton-removal refactor).
- `flutter_rust_bridge.yaml`: root config; `dart_output: .frb-staging/lib/src/rust`.
- `scripts/frb-{stage,generate,check}.sh` and matching `just` recipes.
- `.github/workflows/frb-codegen.yml`: codeowner-gated workflow that clones the orphan branch, regenerates, vendors the wrapper crate (rewrites the `whitenoise` dep from path to a git rev), and force-pushes the orphan branch when something changed.
- `docs/frb-flutter-migration.md`: architecture, bootstrap, rollout sequence, Flutter-side cleanup checklist.

## NOT on master

The Flutter package shape (pubspec, cargokit, platform glue, generated dart, vendored rust source) lives only on the `flutter-package` orphan branch (no shared history with master). Local dev uses `.frb-staging/` (gitignored) as a worktree of that branch.

## Codeowner gate

Hardcoded allowlist in the workflow (mirror `.github/CODEOWNERS`): @erskingardner, @dannym-arx, @mubarakcoded, @jgmontoya. Non-codeowner pushes skip the codegen job; the orphan branch stays put.

## Coordination with the Flutter side

This PR's wrapper sources came from `whitenoise.move-frb-out`'s `rust/src/api/`. Once this PR lands and CI updates the orphan branch, a separate Flutter-side PR (per `docs/frb-flutter-migration.md`) removes `rust/`, `rust_builder/`, `flutter_rust_bridge.yaml`, `lib/src/rust/`, the `just generate` recipe, and switches the pubspec to a git dep on the `flutter-package` ref.

## Verified locally

- `cargo check -p rust_lib_whitenoise`: wrapper compiles.
- `just frb-check`: wrapper passes clippy under `-D warnings`.
- `just check-fmt`: fmt clean.
- `just frb-stage && just frb-generate`: end-to-end codegen run; idempotent on rerun.

## Not yet verified

- First `workflow_dispatch` run end-to-end (proves the orphan-branch update path).
- Flutter app consuming the orphan branch via `flutter pub get`.

## Suggested rollout

1. Run the workflow once via `workflow_dispatch` to prove the codegen and orphan-branch update path.
2. Verify by cloning the orphan branch and running `flutter pub get` in a throwaway Flutter app.
3. Land the Flutter cleanup PR.

Draft until step 1 and 2 are green.

issue.title: Recover some coverage on account DB wrappers and membership ops
issue.body:
## Summary

The arch-refactor merge dropped CI coverage 94.95% → 89.02%. This PR adds 8 targeted unit tests covering paths the refactor introduced without tests — three new per-account-DB repositories and the lightweight column-flip behavior of `MembershipOpsForGroup::archive` / `unarchive`.

## What's tested

`database/account/push_registrations.rs` (2 tests)
- `upsert_binds_repo_account_pubkey_to_returned_registration` — the wrapper's only added behavior is binding `account_pubkey`; this locks it in.
- `separate_accounts_have_independent_per_account_dbs` — the per-account-DB architectural invariant (post-#786 split); two repos over distinct account DBs must not see each other's rows. Inner `PushRegistration` tests share one pool and can't express this.

`database/account/group_push_tokens.rs` (1 test)
- `upsert_binds_repo_account_pubkey_to_returned_token` — pubkey-binding contract on the wrapper.

`database/account/published_key_packages.rs` (1 test)
- `mark_key_material_deleted_by_id_flips_one_row_only` — contrapositive regression guard for PR #822: the by-id variant must NOT cascade to dual-kind twins. A future refactor that "fixes consistency" by accidentally hash_ref-scoping the by-id variant trips this test. No inner-test analogue.

`accounts_groups.rs` (4 tests)
- `test_archive_sets_archived_at`, `test_archive_is_idempotent`, `test_unarchive_clears_archived_at`, `test_unarchive_on_unarchived_chat_is_no_op` — lightweight column-flip tests for `MembershipOpsForGroup::archive`/`unarchive` via the `get_or_create(None)` path. Distinct from the existing `chat_list.rs` archive tests, which spin up a real MLS group via `create_group(...)` and assert stream emit; these target the wrapper's mutation contract without the MLS setup cost.

## What's deliberately not in this PR

- **Wrapper pure-delegation roundtrip tests.** Pure pass-through `Ok(Inner::fn(...).await?)` calls add coverage but no signal — the inner SQL has its own tests. Per the user rule "tests that really increase coverage, not tests that are not testing anything," these were dropped after review.
- **Hash_ref-scoped twin tests** for `mark_consumed` / `mark_key_material_deleted_by_hash_ref`. Already covered by the inner tests `test_mark_consumed_updates_timestamp_for_twins` and `test_mark_key_material_deleted_by_hash_ref_marks_twins` in `database/published_key_packages.rs`.
- **Archive/unarchive emit-frame tests.** Already covered at the heavyweight level by `test_archive_chat_emits_to_both_stream_channels` in `chat_list.rs`.
- **Schema-shadowing fix.** The account-DB tests currently hand-roll a `DROP TABLE + CREATE TABLE` because `AccountDatabase::new` uses `open_without_migrations` (running the full timeline here would require wiring a shared pool). Filed for a separate follow-up — a `setup_account_db_with_migrations()` helper that the whole `account/*.rs` suite can migrate to.

## Coverage math caveat

Coverage probably lands around 90–92% local lib — clears the post-merge CI baseline of 89.02% but doesn't recover the full pre-merge 94.95%. The remaining gap is structural: arch-refactor genuinely deleted code paths that had coverage, and shallow tests aren't the right fix.

## Verification

- `just check-fmt` ✓
- `just check-clippy` ✓
- `cargo test --lib whitenoise::database::account` — 55 pass
- `cargo test --lib whitenoise::accounts_groups::tests` — all pass including the 4 new archive/unarchive

![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/fe803ca425e08f2909f8cd21fb03cb058c6ba39e24b854f51ae047c3c37d5384.png)

## What changed

FRB codegen runs in whitenoise-rs CI now. Every codeowner push to `master` regenerates the Dart bindings and pushes them to a dedicated `flutter-package` orphan branch. The Flutter app consumes that branch as a normal git dependency.

No more `flutter_rust_bridge_codegen generate` runs on the Flutter side. No more git-rev bumps after Rust API changes.

## Added on master

- `crates/whitenoise-frb/`: the FFI wrapper crate. Workspace member, path dep on the parent `whitenoise` crate. Sources ported from the in-flight `whitenoise.move-frb-out` branch (post-singleton-removal refactor).
- `flutter_rust_bridge.yaml`: root config; `dart_output: .frb-staging/lib/src/rust`.
- `scripts/frb-{stage,generate,check}.sh` and matching `just` recipes.
- `.github/workflows/frb-codegen.yml`: codeowner-gated workflow that clones the orphan branch, regenerates, vendors the wrapper crate (rewrites the `whitenoise` dep from path to a git rev), and force-pushes the orphan branch when something changed.
- `docs/frb-flutter-migration.md`: architecture, bootstrap, rollout sequence, Flutter-side cleanup checklist.

## NOT on master

The Flutter package shape (pubspec, cargokit, platform glue, generated dart, vendored rust source) lives only on the `flutter-package` orphan branch (no shared history with master). Local dev uses `.frb-staging/` (gitignored) as a worktree of that branch.

## Codeowner gate

Hardcoded allowlist in the workflow (mirror `.github/CODEOWNERS`): @erskingardner, @dannym-arx, @mubarakcoded, @jgmontoya. Non-codeowner pushes skip the codegen job; the orphan branch stays put.

## Coordination with the Flutter side

This PR's wrapper sources came from `whitenoise.move-frb-out`'s `rust/src/api/`. Once this PR lands and CI updates the orphan branch, a separate Flutter-side PR (per `docs/frb-flutter-migration.md`) removes `rust/`, `rust_builder/`, `flutter_rust_bridge.yaml`, `lib/src/rust/`, the `just generate` recipe, and switches the pubspec to a git dep on the `flutter-package` ref.

## Verified locally

- `cargo check -p rust_lib_whitenoise`: wrapper compiles.
- `just frb-check`: wrapper passes clippy under `-D warnings`.
- `just check-fmt`: fmt clean.
- `just frb-stage && just frb-generate`: end-to-end codegen run; idempotent on rerun.

## Not yet verified

- First `workflow_dispatch` run end-to-end (proves the orphan-branch update path).
- Flutter app consuming the orphan branch via `flutter pub get`.

## Suggested rollout

1. Run the workflow once via `workflow_dispatch` to prove the codegen and orphan-branch update path.
2. Verify by cloning the orphan branch and running `flutter pub get` in a throwaway Flutter app.
3. Land the Flutter cleanup PR.

Draft until step 1 and 2 are green.

A marmot used to scurry between two burrows ferrying every Rust API change by paw. Now the burrow does it.

```yaml
  working-directory: source
  run: echo "sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
```
Then reference `${{ steps.source_sha.outputs.sha }}` (or `$SOURCE_SHA` from an env var set in that step) everywhere instead of `${{ github.sha }}`.

---

## 🟠 High

### 2. `crates/whitenoise-frb/` is invisible to standard CI clippy

**File:** `scripts/check-clippy.sh`

```bash
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --no-deps -- -D warnings ...
```

Without `--workspace`, this only lints the *default package* — the root `whitenoise` crate. `crates/whitenoise-frb/` is a separate workspace member and is **never checked** by the standard CI pipeline (PRs, pushes from non-codeowners). Wrapper crate compilation failures or clippy errors in PRs won't surface until a codeowner lands a commit to master and the `frb-codegen.yml` workflow runs.

**Fix:** Either add `--workspace` to `check-clippy.sh`, or add a separate CI job that runs `frb-check.sh` on every PR:
```bash
# Option A — extend existing script
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --no-deps -- -D warnings ...

# Option B — add a separate CI step/job triggered on PRs that touch crates/whitenoise-frb/**
```

### 3. Hardcoded codeowner allowlist will drift

**File:** `.github/workflows/frb-codegen.yml`, lines 26–30

```bash
codeowners=(erskingardner dannym-arx mubarakcoded jgmontoya)
```

This list must be manually kept in sync with `.github/CODEOWNERS`. There's no safeguard against drift (e.g., a new codeowner added to `CODEOWNERS` but not the workflow, or a departed member removed from one but not the other). The docs acknowledge this, but it's a maintenance footgun.

**Fix:** Read CODEOWNERS dynamically at runtime, or use a CODEOWNERS-aware action. A lightweight option:
```bash
# Extract from CODEOWNERS (adjust pattern to match your format)
mapfile -t codeowners < <(grep -E '^\*\s+' .github/CODEOWNERS | awk '{for(i=2;i<=NF;i++) gsub(/@/,"",$i); for(i=2;i<=NF;i++) print $i}')
```
Or use the [`@nickelc/codeowners-check`](https://github.com/nickelc/codeowners-check) action.

### 4. `workflow_dispatch` grants any write-access user push rights to `flutter-package`

**File:** `.github/workflows/frb-codegen.yml`, lines 33–36

```bash
if [[ "$EVENT" == "workflow_dispatch" ]]; then
  echo "Manual dispatch by $ACTOR — bypassing actor check."
  echo "authorized=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
```

Anyone with repository write access (Contributors, Triage+ on public repos, or Collaborators on private) can trigger `workflow_dispatch` and get an unconditional `authorized=true`, bypassing the allowlist entirely. The intended guarantee is "codeowners only touch `flutter-package`", but this creates a wider escape hatch.

**Fix:** Apply the same allowlist check for `workflow_dispatch`, or require it to be triggerable only by specific actors using OIDC/environment protection rules on a dedicated environment:
```bash
# Same check for both event types:
for owner in "${codeowners[@]}"; do
  if [[ "$ACTOR" == "$owner" ]]; then
    echo "authorized=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    exit 0
  fi
done
echo "authorized=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
```

---

## 🟡 Medium

### 5. Token embedded in git remote URL

**File:** `.github/workflows/frb-codegen.yml`, "Commit and push" step

```bash
git remote set-url origin "https://x-access-token:${GH_TOKEN}@github.com/${REPO}.git"
```

This embeds the token in the remote URL, where it can appear in `git remote -v`, git credential files, and in workflow debug logs if step debugging is enabled. GitHub Actions does mask secret values in logs, but the URL form can bypass masking in some edge cases.

**Fix:** Use a transient credential helper instead:
```bash
git config --local credential.helper '!f() { echo "username=x-access-token"; echo "password='"${GH_TOKEN}"'"; }; f'
git push origin flutter-package
```
Or use the `gh` CLI which handles authentication transparently: `gh auth setup-git && git push origin flutter-package`.

### 6. Silent fetch failure in `frb-stage.sh`

**File:** `scripts/frb-stage.sh`, lines 20–23

```bash
git -C "${STAGING}" fetch --quiet origin "${BRANCH}" || true
if git -C "${STAGING}" rev-parse "@{upstream}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    git -C "${STAGING}" reset --hard "@{upstream}"
fi
```

If the fetch fails (network issue, expired credentials), `|| true` swallows the error. The `reset --hard "@{upstream}"` then silently resets to a *stale* tracking ref. A developer running `just frb-stage` after a fetch failure gets no warning and works against stale content.

**Fix:**
```bash
if ! git -C "${STAGING}" fetch --quiet origin "${BRANCH}"; then
    echo "warning: fetch failed — reset will use cached upstream ref (may be stale)" >&2
fi
```

### 7. `frb-check.sh` does not check formatting

**File:** `scripts/frb-check.sh`

The script only runs clippy. Since `frb-generate.sh` runs `cargo fmt 2>/dev/null || true` (silently), and the standard `check-fmt.sh` only covers the root crate, formatting drift in the wrapper crate is never caught in CI. Generated Dart is formatted with `dart format`, but the generated Rust side in `.frb-staging/rust/` is not validated.

**Fix:** Add a fmt check for the wrapper:
```bash
cargo fmt --package rust_lib_whitenoise --check
```

### 8. `cargo fmt` errors silently swallowed in `frb-generate.sh`

**File:** `scripts/frb-generate.sh`, line 47

```bash
cargo fmt --package rust_lib_whitenoise 2>/dev/null || true
```

Both stderr and the exit code are suppressed. If `cargo fmt` fails (e.g., malformed generated Rust), the local developer gets no signal.

**Fix:**
```bash
if command -v cargo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "Formatting generated Rust file..."
    cargo fmt --package rust_lib_whitenoise || echo "warning: cargo fmt failed on generated Rust" >&2
fi
```

---

## 🔵 Low

### 9. `sed` rewrite failure produces an unhelpful error message

**File:** `.github/workflows/frb-codegen.yml`, "Vendor wrapper crate" step

The validation grep after the sed rewrite:
```bash
if grep -q 'path = "../.."' "${STAGING}/rust/Cargo.toml"; then
  echo "Dep rewrite failed — Cargo.toml still references path = ../.." >&2
  exit 1
fi
```

This is good — it catches a no-op sed. But the error message doesn't show what the file looks like, making CI debugging painful. Also, `grep -q 'path = "../.."'` would false-positive if *any other dependency* uses a relative path (unlikely here but worth hardening).

**Fix:**
```bash
if grep -q '^whitenoise = { path = ' "${STAGING}/rust/Cargo.toml"; then
  echo "Dep rewrite failed. Cargo.toml content:" >&2
  cat "${STAGING}/rust/Cargo.toml" >&2
  exit 1
fi
```

### 10. Bootstrap instructions use hardcoded `/tmp/fp-bootstrap`

**File:** `docs/frb-flutter-migration.md`

```sh
git worktree add --orphan -b flutter-package /tmp/fp-bootstrap
```

`/tmp` may not exist on all systems (Windows, some Docker images) and `/tmp` path collisions are possible on shared CI machines. The `ln -s /tmp/fp-bootstrap .frb-staging` symlink approach also means `just frb-generate` runs with `flutter_rust_bridge.yaml`'s `dart_output` resolving through a symlink, which some tools handle inconsistently.

**Fix:** Use `mktemp -d` and a real worktree:
```sh
BOOTSTRAP_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
git worktree add --orphan -b flutter-package "$BOOTSTRAP_DIR"
# ... seed files ...
git worktree add .frb-staging flutter-package  # real worktree, not symlink
just frb-generate
```

---

## ✅ Things done well

- **Concurrency guard** (`cancel-in-progress: false`) prevents concurrent orphan-branch force-pushes — correct choice.
- **`frb-stage.sh` branch safety check**: refuses to clobber a worktree on the wrong branch. Nice defensive programming.
- **Dep rewrite validation**: the grep-after-sed pattern catches silent sed failures and exits non-zero.
- **`flutter_rust_bridge_codegen` version pinned** identically in `frb-generate.sh`, CI workflow, and `crates/whitenoise-frb/Cargo.toml` — good lockstep.
- **`REGENERATED.txt` provenance** with source SHA, run ID, timestamp, and FRB version is excellent for debugging "which Rust commit generated these bindings".
- **Orphan branch model** keeps master Rust-only and avoids the "bump rev + re-run codegen" Flutter-side chore entirely.
- **`rust-toolchain.toml`** pins `1.90.0` consistently with the CI workflow toolchain install — no ambient-toolchain surprises.
- **`frb-generate.sh` version mismatch check** is a good local DX guard.

issue.title: Recover some coverage on account DB wrappers and membership ops
issue.body:
## Summary

The arch-refactor merge dropped CI coverage 94.95% → 89.02%. This PR adds 8 targeted unit tests covering paths the refactor introduced without tests — three new per-account-DB repositories and the lightweight column-flip behavior of `MembershipOpsForGroup::archive` / `unarchive`.

## What's tested

`database/account/push_registrations.rs` (2 tests)
- `upsert_binds_repo_account_pubkey_to_returned_registration` — the wrapper's only added behavior is binding `account_pubkey`; this locks it in.
- `separate_accounts_have_independent_per_account_dbs` — the per-account-DB architectural invariant (post-#786 split); two repos over distinct account DBs must not see each other's rows. Inner `PushRegistration` tests share one pool and can't express this.

`database/account/group_push_tokens.rs` (1 test)
- `upsert_binds_repo_account_pubkey_to_returned_token` — pubkey-binding contract on the wrapper.

`database/account/published_key_packages.rs` (1 test)
- `mark_key_material_deleted_by_id_flips_one_row_only` — contrapositive regression guard for PR #822: the by-id variant must NOT cascade to dual-kind twins. A future refactor that "fixes consistency" by accidentally hash_ref-scoping the by-id variant trips this test. No inner-test analogue.

`accounts_groups.rs` (4 tests)
- `test_archive_sets_archived_at`, `test_archive_is_idempotent`, `test_unarchive_clears_archived_at`, `test_unarchive_on_unarchived_chat_is_no_op` — lightweight column-flip tests for `MembershipOpsForGroup::archive`/`unarchive` via the `get_or_create(None)` path. Distinct from the existing `chat_list.rs` archive tests, which spin up a real MLS group via `create_group(...)` and assert stream emit; these target the wrapper's mutation contract without the MLS setup cost.

## What's deliberately not in this PR

- **Wrapper pure-delegation roundtrip tests.** Pure pass-through `Ok(Inner::fn(...).await?)` calls add coverage but no signal — the inner SQL has its own tests. Per the user rule "tests that really increase coverage, not tests that are not testing anything," these were dropped after review.
- **Hash_ref-scoped twin tests** for `mark_consumed` / `mark_key_material_deleted_by_hash_ref`. Already covered by the inner tests `test_mark_consumed_updates_timestamp_for_twins` and `test_mark_key_material_deleted_by_hash_ref_marks_twins` in `database/published_key_packages.rs`.
- **Archive/unarchive emit-frame tests.** Already covered at the heavyweight level by `test_archive_chat_emits_to_both_stream_channels` in `chat_list.rs`.
- **Schema-shadowing fix.** The account-DB tests currently hand-roll a `DROP TABLE + CREATE TABLE` because `AccountDatabase::new` uses `open_without_migrations` (running the full timeline here would require wiring a shared pool). Filed for a separate follow-up — a `setup_account_db_with_migrations()` helper that the whole `account/*.rs` suite can migrate to.

## Coverage math caveat

Coverage probably lands around 90–92% local lib — clears the post-merge CI baseline of 89.02% but doesn't recover the full pre-merge 94.95%. The remaining gap is structural: arch-refactor genuinely deleted code paths that had coverage, and shallow tests aren't the right fix.

## Verification

- `just check-fmt` ✓
- `just check-clippy` ✓
- `cargo test --lib whitenoise::database::account` — 55 pass
- `cargo test --lib whitenoise::accounts_groups::tests` — all pass including the 4 new archive/unarchive

issue.title: feat(frb): move FRB codegen into whitenoise-rs
issue.body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/fe803ca425e08f2909f8cd21fb03cb058c6ba39e24b854f51ae047c3c37d5384.png)

## What changed

FRB codegen runs in whitenoise-rs CI now. Every codeowner push to `master` regenerates the Dart bindings and pushes them to a dedicated `flutter-package` orphan branch. The Flutter app consumes that branch as a normal git dependency.

No more `flutter_rust_bridge_codegen generate` runs on the Flutter side. No more git-rev bumps after Rust API changes.

## Added on master

- `crates/whitenoise-frb/`: the FFI wrapper crate. Workspace member, path dep on the parent `whitenoise` crate. Sources ported from the in-flight `whitenoise.move-frb-out` branch (post-singleton-removal refactor).
- `flutter_rust_bridge.yaml`: root config; `dart_output: .frb-staging/lib/src/rust`.
- `scripts/frb-{stage,generate,check}.sh` and matching `just` recipes.
- `.github/workflows/frb-codegen.yml`: codeowner-gated workflow that clones the orphan branch, regenerates, vendors the wrapper crate (rewrites the `whitenoise` dep from path to a git rev), and force-pushes the orphan branch when something changed.
- `docs/frb-flutter-migration.md`: architecture, bootstrap, rollout sequence, Flutter-side cleanup checklist.

## NOT on master

The Flutter package shape (pubspec, cargokit, platform glue, generated dart, vendored rust source) lives only on the `flutter-package` orphan branch (no shared history with master). Local dev uses `.frb-staging/` (gitignored) as a worktree of that branch.

## Codeowner gate

Hardcoded allowlist in the workflow (mirror `.github/CODEOWNERS`): @erskingardner, @dannym-arx, @mubarakcoded, @jgmontoya. Non-codeowner pushes skip the codegen job; the orphan branch stays put.

## Coordination with the Flutter side

This PR's wrapper sources came from `whitenoise.move-frb-out`'s `rust/src/api/`. Once this PR lands and CI updates the orphan branch, a separate Flutter-side PR (per `docs/frb-flutter-migration.md`) removes `rust/`, `rust_builder/`, `flutter_rust_bridge.yaml`, `lib/src/rust/`, the `just generate` recipe, and switches the pubspec to a git dep on the `flutter-package` ref.

## Verified locally

- `cargo check -p rust_lib_whitenoise`: wrapper compiles.

issue.body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/fe803ca425e08f2909f8cd21fb03cb058c6ba39e24b854f51ae047c3c37d5384.png)

## What changed

FRB codegen runs in whitenoise-rs CI now. Every codeowner push to `master` regenerates the Dart bindings and pushes them to a dedicated `flutter-package` orphan branch. The Flutter app consumes that branch as a normal git dependency.

No more `flutter_rust_bridge_codegen generate` runs on the Flutter side. No more git-rev bumps after Rust API changes.

## Added on master

- `crates/whitenoise-frb/`: the FFI wrapper crate. Workspace member, path dep on the parent `whitenoise` crate. Sources ported from the in-flight `whitenoise.move-frb-out` branch (post-singleton-removal refactor).
- `flutter_rust_bridge.yaml`: root config; `dart_output: .frb-staging/lib/src/rust`.
- `scripts/frb-{stage,generate,check}.sh` and matching `just` recipes.
- `.github/workflows/frb-codegen.yml`: codeowner-gated workflow that clones the orphan branch, regenerates, vendors the wrapper crate (rewrites the `whitenoise` dep from path to a git rev), and force-pushes the orphan branch when something changed.
- `docs/frb-flutter-migration.md`: architecture, bootstrap, rollout sequence, Flutter-side cleanup checklist.

## NOT on master

The Flutter package shape (pubspec, cargokit, platform glue, generated dart, vendored rust source) lives only on the `flutter-package` orphan branch (no shared history with master). Local dev uses `.frb-staging/` (gitignored) as a worktree of that branch.

## Codeowner gate

Hardcoded allowlist in the workflow (mirror `.github/CODEOWNERS`): @erskingardner, @dannym-arx, @mubarakcoded, @jgmontoya. Non-codeowner pushes skip the codegen job; the orphan branch stays put.

## Coordination with the Flutter side

This PR's wrapper sources came from `whitenoise.move-frb-out`'s `rust/src/api/`. Once this PR lands and CI updates the orphan branch, a separate Flutter-side PR (per `docs/frb-flutter-migration.md`) removes `rust/`, `rust_builder/`, `flutter_rust_bridge.yaml`, `lib/src/rust/`, the `just generate` recipe, and switches the pubspec to a git dep on the `flutter-package` ref.

## Verified locally

- `cargo check -p rust_lib_whitenoise`: wrapper compiles.
- `just frb-check`: wrapper passes clippy under `-D warnings`.
- `just check-fmt`: fmt clean.
- `just frb-stage && just frb-generate`: end-to-end codegen run; idempotent on rerun.

## Not yet verified

- First `workflow_dispatch` run end-to-end (proves the orphan-branch update path).
- Flutter app consuming the orphan branch via `flutter pub get`.

## Suggested rollout

1. Run the workflow once via `workflow_dispatch` to prove the codegen and orphan-branch update path.
2. Verify by cloning the orphan branch and running `flutter pub get` in a throwaway Flutter app.
3. Land the Flutter cleanup PR.

Draft until step 1 and 2 are green.

A marmot used to scurry between two burrows ferrying every Rust API change by paw. Now the burrow does it.
